$comment: iOS-SPECIFIC tokens. The shared design — colours, spacing, radii, curves, type scale — lives in the hub and reaches here through `design/tokens.json`. This file carries only what makes sense on iOS alone, and it is ASSEMBLED with the hub at generation time. A shared token landing here would be a divergence in the making: the website would never see it.

icon.$comment: SF Symbol and illustration sizes, in points. Not shared with the website: there an icon is an SVG sized by its container, here it is a font whose size is declared.

stroke.$comment: Stroke widths. `hairline` is half a point: on a 3× screen that is one and a half pixels — the thinnest line that still renders crisply.

elevation.$comment: Shadows, by role rather than by value. A shadow is described by three numbers that only mean anything together: splitting them invites changing one alone.

opacity.$comment: Opacities named by what they mean. `tintOnMaterial` is the iOS 18 fallback's: a tint laid over a translucent material, enough to be seen, not enough to hide the blur.

duration.$comment: Animation durations, in seconds. The CURVES are shared with the website: the curve carries the feel, the duration tunes it to the medium. A touch screen has less patience than a web page.

layout.$comment: `readingWidth` bounds the text column: a line reads well at around 65 characters, and expressing it as a multiple of the body size makes it follow the type scale. `pressedScale` lives here and not under `opacity` — it is a scale factor, not a transparency, and filing it in the wrong place leads somebody to write `opacity(Tokens.Opacity.pressed)` one day.
